nih.rationale: The study is a single-centre retrospective cohort with a clear question (Q1), a well-defined consecutive population (Q2, Q3, Q4), well-described and consistently applied exposure (optimal vs. standard PEEP strategy; Q9) that was re-assessed daily (Q10), well-defined outcomes including an objective echo-based primary outcome and mortality endpoints (Q11), essentially complete follow-up (Q13), and multivariable adjustment for age, hypertension, diabetes and admission period (Q14). It is downgraded from Good, but not to Poor, by two items: Q5 (no sample-size justification, power description or a priori variance/effect estimate - explicitly not a fatal flaw per the tool) and Q12 (blinding of outcome assessors is not reported; data were collected by two of the study authors, relevant because the primary outcome is an echocardiographic interpretation and inotrope decision). Additional concern, acknowledged by the authors, is residual confounding by co-interventions that changed in step with the exposure - proning on ECMO (22.7% vs. 0%) and a higher BMI in the optimal-PEEP group - which was not statistically adjusted for, together with the calendar-time (before/after) structure of the comparison; these lower confidence in the association without constituting a fatal design flaw.
